results.title: Characters of a finite abelian group have absolute value one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $\psi$ be an additive character of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$, that is, a map $\psi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\psi(0) = 1$ and $\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$. Then $|\psi(x)| = 1$ for every $x \in G$.

results.title: Squared-norm Plancherel identity for the finite Fourier transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $\sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 = |G| \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$, where $\psi$ runs over all additive characters of $G$.

results.title: Pointwise bound from a small Fourier support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that the discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $x \in G$, $|f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|B|}{|G|} \sum_{y \in G} |f(y)|^2$.

results.title: Concentration bound for a function with small Fourier support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that the discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $A \subseteq G$, $\sum_{x \in A} |f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$.

results.title: Concentration bound for the Fourier transform of a function with small support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A \subseteq G$, let $B$ be any set of additive characters of $G$, and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanish outside $A$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $\sum_{\psi \in B} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2$, where the last sum runs over all additive characters $\psi$ of $G$.

results.title: Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a nonzero function with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $|G| \le |\{x \in G : f(x) \neq 0\}| \cdot |\{\psi : \hat f(\psi) \neq 0\}|$, where $\psi$ ranges over the additive characters of $G$.

results.title: Functions with small support and small Fourier support vanish
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A \subseteq G$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ with $|A| \cdot |B| < |G|$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanishes outside $A$ and its discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$, then $f = 0$.

results.title: Erdős–Lovász family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers is an Erdős–Lovász family of order $n$ when every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ (not necessarily distinct) have a common element, and every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 21 (Erdős–Lovász)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers in which every member has exactly $n$ elements, any two members have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$. This expresses $f(n) \ll n$, where $f(n)$ is the least size of such a family.

results.title: Kahn's theorem on the Erdős–Lovász problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers with the following properties: every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$.

results.title: Instances of HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED)
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) is a pair $(n, E)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a finite list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges.

results.title: Graph of a HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an instance $(n, E)$, its graph is the simple graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$.

results.title: Well-formed HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is well formed when $0 < n$, the list $E$ has no repeated entries, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.

results.title: Feasible HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is feasible when $n \ge 3$ and its graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, that is, a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once.

results.title: HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a well-formed instance $(n, E)$ with $n \ge 3$ whose graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.

results.title: HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.summary: The instance with numbers $a_1, \dots, a_r$ and target $t$ is encoded as the block of $t$ followed by the blocks of $a_1, \dots, a_r$ in order. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $S$ be the insertion sort of $L$ in nondecreasing order, and let $k$ be a natural number. If $k < |L|$, quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns the entry of $S$ at zero-based position $k$; if $k \ge |L|$, it returns no element.

results.title: Rank inequalities determine the quickselect value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linear order, let $k$ be a natural number and let $x$ be an element. Counting entries of $L$ with multiplicity, if the number of entries less than $x$ is at most $k$ and $k$ is less than the number of entries at most $x$, then quickselect on $L$ with zero-based rank $k$ returns $x$.

results.title: Worst-case comparison bound for quickselect
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ over a linear order, of length $n$, and every natural number $k$, quickselect on $L$ with rank $k$ makes at most $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
